conviction_note: The bar is the company's own guide: FY26 adjusted EBITDA 'toward the lower end' of $380-410M means Q4 needs about $98M (Q3 was $99M, Q4 FY25 $90M), and the reaffirmed $90-110M FCF means Q4 needs $58-78M of FCF. The evidence leans mildly negative on the FCF test: a sibling packager (Amcor) took a $1.13B working-capital outflow on resin in the same Jul-Sep quarter, European PP was still around EUR 1,950/t in August, and Magnera's raw-material inventory was already rising. Against that, Q4 is seasonally the cash quarter (record $96M OCF a year ago), capex runs about $15M a quarter, and a first FY27 guide comes with about $20M of synergy/CORE carryover. Coverage is thin (1-2 analysts) and the name sold off 7.5% on 'tight cash flow' last quarter, so the move is set large (8%) with p_up 45; scaled = (0.90-1) x 8 = -0.8 against an impact_sum of -1.5, the gap being the FY27 guide's unknown sign.

positioning_check: Short interest is about 1.8M shares with 4.3 days to cover as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, down from 2.0M / 5.5 days (Oct 2) and 2.3M / 6.4 days (Aug 20) (https://massive.com/quote/magn.md ; https://equibles.com/stocks/magn/shortinterest). findings.finding: Cash is the test. FY26 FCF guidance of $90-110M (reaffirmed Aug 5) against YTD FCF of $32M means Q4 must produce $58-78M of FCF ($74-94M of OCF on about $15M of capex). The CFO said 'there's still work to go' on working capital in Q4, and the Q3 10-Q shows raw-material inventory rising to $201M from $171M. The Jul-Sep quarter Magnera is reporting saw continued resin and energy inflation at a direct sibling: Amcor (owner of the former Berry packaging businesses) reported a $1.13B working-capital outflow 'driven by resin price volatility tied to the Middle East conflict' and a guidance cut on late-quarter energy and distribution costs. So the risk is an FCF result at or below the low end, or a FY26 FCF miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Q3 print the stock closed down about 7.5% at $12.53 on Aug 7, 2026, with the move attributed to the 'tight' FCF outlook despite the best EBITDA since the merger (https://www.webull.com/news/15358933241242624). NB: the sealed baseline records this event as +3.03, and that sign is disputed. On the Q4 FY25 print the stock rose about 28% after hours on a record $96M Q4 OCF and FCF above target (https://www.itiger.com/news/2584902145).
findings.why_not_priced: The company reaffirmed the FCF range, and there is no Street FCF estimate on any aggregator, so the implied Q4 requirement ($58-78M, about 2x any prior FY26 quarter combined) is not on any wire. Amcor's working-capital outflow came out on 2026-11-04 in a different company's release. If this were priced, the stock would not have been at $12.6-13.2 in mid-November, up from $10.62 in mid-October.
findings.independence: Amcor Q1 FY27 (Sep quarter): $1.13B working-capital outflow on resin volatility, raw-material pass-through about +8% of sales, guide cut on energy costs (https://247wallst.com/cards/amcor-q1-2027-earnings-amcr-01m6m9er57pay69akaea7r12ca, 2026-11-04). Ontex (hygiene customer) said raw material and transport costs ran about 10% above the start-of-year level in Q3 (https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/stock-news/ontex-lowers-ebitda-forecast-to-eur143-148m-third-quarter-ebitda-down-49/28017.html, 2026-10-28). Both are proxies. Against: Q4 FY25 OCF was a record $96M, and Magnera uses non-recourse supply-chain-finance receivable sales that can pull cash forward (10-Q).

findings.finding: The Q4 EBITDA bar from the guide is about $98M ($380M low end less $282M YTD), against $99M in Q3 and $90M in Q4 FY25. The CEO said Q4 demand would be 'more of the same' as Q3. Americas price-cost was neutral and Rest of World (Europe) had 'a lag of a couple million dollars that will carry into Q4'. European resin was still elevated through Magnera's Q4: PP injection grade about EUR 1,950-1,955/t FD NWE in August, flat week on week, and propylene contract reportedly up EUR 55/t in August. So the RoW lag likely did not unwind and Q4 lands at or slightly below the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3's EBITDA beat (+9% y/y, $99M) with the guide moved to the low end was sold about 7.5% (webull, 2026-08-07). This name has not paid for EBITDA alone.
findings.why_not_priced: The low end is already guided, so most of this is inside what the company told the market. The incremental part is that European resin stayed high through August, which is visible only in trade-press price assessments (Polymerupdate) that the 1-2 analysts covering a $420M-cap name are unlikely to model monthly. A priced RoW miss would show up as estimate cuts; Chartmill's snippet shows next-quarter EPS revised up about 16% over three months instead.
findings.independence: European PP contract levels: https://polymerupdate.com/News/Details/1504732 (2026-08-21). Ontex Q3 raw materials about 10% above the start of year (ideal-investisseur, 2026-10-28). US side: StoneX said PP contract rebounded +3 cpp in July and was expected lower in August (https://www.stonex.com/en-us/insights/bi-weekly-plastics-report-august-7-2026/, 2026-08-07), so the Americas lag may have turned favorable, which offsets part of this. This shares the price-cost theme with finding 1 but lands on EBITDA, not cash.

findings.finding: This is the first FY27 guide. Pieces the company has put on the record: about $20M of run-rate synergies and Project CORE benefits 'floating over' into FY27 (CFO, Q3 call), and a new five-layer blown-film line at Dombühl entering commercial production in October 2026. A direct sibling, Amcor, said on 2026-11-04 that it does not expect the higher energy and distribution costs to affect its 2027 results and that it expects double-digit EPS growth in 2027. A FY27 EBITDA range around $400M+ (FY26 about $380M plus about $20M carryover) is plausible, but there is no FY27 consensus to measure it against.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the last first-year guide (FY26 EBITDA $380-410M, FCF $90-110M, 2025-11-19) the stock rose about 28% after hours from a depressed $7.96 (https://www.itiger.com/news/2584902145). The baseline also carries +27.89% for that event.
findings.why_not_priced: The CFO declined to give FY27 guidance in August, and no FY27 EBITDA consensus appears on any aggregator, so the market's FY27 anchor is unknowable from here. The sign is genuinely open, which is why the range is wide and the point is small.
findings.independence: Dombühl line release, 2026-10-05: https://finviz.com/news/398805/magnera-announces-successful-commissioning-of-new-blown-film-production-line-in-dombuhl-germany . Amcor 2027 commentary: https://247wallst.com/cards/amcor-q1-2027-earnings-amcr-01m6m9er57pay69akaea7r12ca . Against: Wells Fargo noted on the Q3 call that the pro forma starting EBITDA was about $445M against about $405M now, a history of guide erosion.

findings.finding: Revenue likely meets or beats the roughly $919M consensus through raw-material pass-through. Amcor's pass-through added about 8% to its Sep-quarter sales, and Ontex said nonwovens costs (Magnera's revenue) ran higher in Q3. Q3 revenue was $857M, flat comparable. The beat is a price pass-through, not volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pass-through revenue has not moved this stock on its own. Q3 revenue of $857M was reported as short of forecast and the stock fell on cash, not sales.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $919M already implies +9.5% y/y, so most of the pass-through is in the number. This is small by construction.
findings.independence: Ontex Q3 2026 (https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/stock-news/ontex-lowers-ebitda-forecast-to-eur143-148m-third-quarter-ebitda-down-49/28017.html). The same Amcor document is used in finding 1, but for a different line (sales, not working capital).

findings.finding: European hygiene customer weakness: Ontex's Q3 2026 total volumes fell 5.1% (baby -9%, feminine -12%). Ontex cut its 2026 EBITDA guide to EUR 143-148M, leverage rose to 3.75x and it is negotiating a covenant waiver. That is soft demand for Magnera's Rest of World hygiene nonwovens and some receivables/credit risk at a customer. Net of the rest of the company: Kimberly-Clark's North America volume rose about 2% in Q3, and Americas is about 55% of Magnera's sales and about 72% of its EBITDA.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RoW EBITDA fell 7% in Q3 and the stock fell about 7.5%, but on cash. There is no isolated RoW reaction on record.
findings.why_not_priced: Ontex's print is a Belgian customer's release, three weeks old, not linked to MAGN on the wire. Magnera already flagged European softness, so this is mostly confirmation.
findings.independence: Kimberly-Clark Q3 2026: NA volume about +2%, International Personal Care organic -4.6% (https://zacks.com/stock/news/3024594/kimberly-clark-q3-earnings-beat-on-lower-interest-costs-sales-miss, 2026-11-05). It points the other way for the Americas.

findings.finding: The annual goodwill impairment test is performed 'as of the first day of the fourth fiscal quarter' (about 2026-06-28). Goodwill and intangibles total $858M against a market cap of roughly $420-450M at the time, and the 10-Q warns that sustained lower multiples 'could result in impairment charges in the future'. A Q4/10-K impairment is possible. It would be non-cash and below EBITDA.

lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy beats inference only in size): the FCF finding rests partly on Amcor/Ontex proxies, so it was trimmed from -1.5 to -1.2; it stays filed because a company number (rising raw-material inventory, the CFO's 'work to go') supports it.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest): the Ontex customer-weakness finding was trimmed from -0.4 to -0.3 against K-C NA volume +2% and Americas' ~72% EBITDA share.
